## Purpose

Part of #57555. Stacked on #57343, so the first two commits here are from that PR.

**Updated 2026-10-05:** the first version timed the default-stream fallback instead of `cuMemcpyBatchAsync`, and inside a server it didn't run at all ([details](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57569#issuecomment-5981553144)). Fixed in a0cc5ad4e; 8eed6a0f4 adds a 5% margin and e26e6e9d4 calibrates on rank 0 only. The numbers below are re-measured inside `vllm serve`.

The CPU→GPU load path picks between `cuMemcpyBatchAsync` and the Triton kernel with two constants tuned on one H100 (`THRESHOLD_BYTES = 28 KiB`, `MIN_N = 16`). The numbers in #57555 (H100, A30, GB10) show that where the two paths cross depends on the copy size, the batch size and the machine, so this lets a worker measure it instead.

With `"calibrate_load_path": true` in `kv_connector_extra_config`, rank 0 times both paths when the offloading worker is created, for its copy sizes, at N = 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, on a dedicated stream like real transfers. Every rank then uses the smallest N from which Triton is more than 5% faster at every larger N; where the two are within 5%, the default decides. If Triton never gets there the handler stays on DMA. The source is the real pinned CPU tensor and the destination is a scratch GPU buffer (at most 16 MiB), so no KV block is written. Copy sizes above 64 KiB would need a bigger scratch and are not measured. If anything goes wrong (no room for the scratch, host region too small, the op raising) the handler keeps the defaults and logs a warning.

The worker init is the natural place for this: the real GPU tensors, the pinned host region and the copy sizes all exist there, the GPU is idle, and `_select_swap_blocks_fn` already runs at that point.

To carry the result, the size cutoff and `MIN_N` are resolved into one `min_n` per handler at init and passed to the Triton wrapper, which still does a single comparison per call. With the option off the values are the same as today, so the default behaviour does not change.

On handlers with more than one copy size (the point @hclsys raised in #57555): one transfer sends all of a handler's sizes in a single call, so the per-size results are reduced to one. I kept that conservative, the largest `min_n`, and DMA for everything if any size never wins on Triton, which is what `max(sizes)` does today. When the sizes disagree the handler logs it, so it is visible how often this happens. Splitting the call by size is left for a follow-up once there is data from a hybrid model.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_swap_blocks_triton.py \
    tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_gpu_worker.py \
    tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_canonical_layout.py \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_canonical_mapping.py \
    tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering -q
pre-commit run --files <the 7 changed files>
```

New tests:

- `test_batches_below_min_n_use_dma`: the wrapper falls back to DMA below the `min_n` it is given (runs without CUDA).
- `test_pick_min_n`: Triton taking over at N=64, ahead everywhere, never ahead, a win at N=32 that doesn't count because N=64 loses again, and cells within the 5% margin left to the default.
- `test_measure_load_paths_times_every_probed_n`: times every probed N on a real pinned tensor, and returns nothing when the host region is too small.
- `test_measure_load_paths_reads_strided_host_rows`: measures on a strided view like the shared offload region (fails on the first version).
- `test_measure_load_paths_avoids_default_stream`: both paths are timed off the default stream (fails on the first version).
- `test_calibrated_load_path_uses_measured_min_n`: the measured value replaces the default, also for a 32 KiB page that defaults to DMA, the handler stays on DMA when Triton never wins, and a size the calibration didn't cover keeps its default.
- `test_calibration_failure_keeps_defaults`: an exception or a skipped measurement leaves `MIN_N`.
- `test_calibration_runs_on_rank0_only`: only rank 0 measures, and every rank gets its result.
- `test_mixed_copy_sizes_reduce_to_one_min_n`: the largest `min_n` is used, and one DMA-only size keeps the handler on DMA.

## Test Result

A30, PCIe Gen4, torch 2.13.0+cu126, Triton 3.7.1, editable install with `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1`, CUDA 12.8 forward-compat libcuda on a 535 kernel driver.

- The test files above: 482 passed, 2 skipped.
- All pre-commit hooks pass on the changed files, including mypy.

The rest is `vllm serve` with Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct TP1 (64 KiB pages) and default flags.

Startup cost. Launch to `/health`, median of 3. Cold means an empty `TRITON_CACHE_DIR`:

| Triton cache | off | on | calibration itself |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| cold | 70.1 s | 70.1 s | 115-121 ms |
| warm | 53.7 s | 53.7 s | 58-63 ms |

No measurable change. The +0.5-1 s I first reported came from a standalone `CPUOffloadingWorker`, where it was mostly the first Triton launch of a fresh process.

What it picked on this GPU, the same in 50 of 50 calibrations per size. N is the number of copies in one load call (blocks × layers); below the cutoff a load stays on DMA.

| copy size | default | calibrated |
|---:|---|---|
| 4 KiB | Triton from N=16 | Triton from N=64 |
| 8 KiB | Triton from N=16 | Triton from N=32 |
| 16 KiB | Triton from N=16 | Triton from N=16 |
| 32 KiB | DMA | Triton from N=128 |
| 64 KiB | DMA | Triton from N=128 |
| 128 KiB | DMA | not measured, DMA |

Serving. Every request loads a 256 MiB prefix from CPU (64 KiB copies: DMA with calibration off, Triton with it on), median of 3 servers:

| | off | on |
|---|---:|---:|
| TTFT, concurrency 1 | 70.3 ms | 63.5 ms |
| TTFT, concurrency 8 | 206 ms | 179 ms |
| requests/s, concurrency 8 | 2.475 | 2.498 |
| TPOT, concurrency 8 | 23.9 ms | 23.8 ms |

Not covered: the measurement runs on an idle GPU, and the Triton path uses GPU compute while the copy engine does not, so under load the real crossover may sit higher. Not measured with TP > 1 serving or on GPUs other than A30. No model eval, since both paths are byte-exact copies and the existing GPU roundtrip tests cover them.

AI assistance (Claude) was used for the implementation, tests and measurements. I reviewed every changed line and ran everything above on my own hardware.

Ran the calibration on GB10 (sm_121, 121.7 GiB unified, aarch64, CUDA 13, torch 2.12.1+cu130), driving `measure_load_paths` / `pick_min_n` directly at `00d8649adc`. This branch touches no C++ against my build base, so the prebuilt `swap_blocks_batch` applies.

It does not return the same answer twice. Same function, same pinned host tensor, same process, seven consecutive calls per size:

```
CALIBRATION_REPS = 5 (as shipped)
   4K   min_n: [64, 64, 32, 64, 16, 64, 64]
  16K   min_n: [32, 16, 256, 32, 16, 64, 256]
  32K   min_n: [256, 16, 32, 32, 256, 64, 64]
  64K   min_n: [32, 16, 16, 128, 128, 256, 128]

CALIBRATION_REPS = 25
   4K   min_n: [64, 32, 32, 32, 16, 16, 16]
  16K   min_n: [16, 32, 16, 16, 16, 16, 16]
  32K   min_n: [32, 32, 16, 16, 16, 64, 64]
  64K   min_n: [128, 256, 128, 32, 32, 32, 128]
```

Five times the reps tightens 16 KiB but not 64 KiB, so this isn't only a rep-count problem.

The underlying medians at 16 KiB, six runs:

```
run   arm    N=16     N=32     N=64     N=128    N=256
0     dma    0.0489   0.0790   0.1292   0.2434   0.5520
0     tri    0.0473   0.0382   0.0381   0.0752   0.0928
3     dma    0.0483   0.0771   0.1261   0.2300   0.4388
3     tri    0.2140   0.1979   0.1275   0.1086   0.1234
```

The DMA arm is steady to about 2%. The Triton arm's median at N=16 moves between 0.037 and 0.25 ms across identical calls, roughly 6x, and it is right at that N that the crossing gets decided.

What I ruled out before blaming variance: the co-tenant on this card holds 16.9 GB but is not computing (utilization sampled at 0-1%), and the SM clock sits at 2411 MHz with the part at 53 C for the whole run, so no throttle. It is not JIT either, since `run_ms` already discards a warm-up and the fast runs are as often first as last.

The reduction then amplifies it. `pick_min_n` walks down from the largest N and breaks on the first `tri > dma`, with no tolerance, so one cell landing the wrong side of 1.0 at N=128 or 256 truncates the whole walk. That is how 16 KiB gets both 16 and 256 out of the same machine minutes apart.

Two things that might help, in the order I'd try them:

- require a margin rather than `tri > dma`, so a cell within noise of parity doesn't break the walk
- repeat the whole measurement two or three times and take the consensus pick, rather than more reps inside one measurement

I also tried a variant with the destination slots permuted instead of contiguous, since real loads write scattered block ids and the contiguous scratch is friendlier to the copy engine than production is. The run-to-run spread above swamps it, so I have nothing to report there yet, and it seems worth settling the stability first.

Caveats: one machine, load direction only, nothing above 64 KiB, and I drove the two functions directly rather than through a real serve, so I have not seen what a handler picks in situ.

re 4, it's the default stream. Ran it on a GB10 (sm_121, unified memory, CUDA 13.0, torch 2.12.1, PR head 5ea23ad).

swap_blocks_batch only takes cuMemcpyBatchAsync when the current stream isn't stream 0 (`usable_stream` in cache_kernels.cu), otherwise it loops cudaMemcpyAsync. I couldn't find anything on the init path that sets a stream, so measure_load_paths times the loop. Checked with VLLM_KV_OFFLOAD_MAX_BATCH_DESCRIPTORS=1 (only chunks the batch path): N=256 x 4 KiB goes 0.128 -> 0.412 ms on a side stream, default stream 0.44 -> 0.49, so it isn't using it.

measure_load_paths as is vs inside `with torch.cuda.stream(torch.cuda.Stream())`, DMA ms at N=16 / N=256:

4 KiB   0.035 / 0.439  vs  0.018 / 0.125
16 KiB  0.033 / 0.424  vs  0.035 / 0.286

Triton arm doesn't move. pick_min_n over 7 runs: 4 KiB gives 16 vs 32 (32-64 in an earlier run), 16 and 24 KiB give 16 both ways.

So here only the 4 KiB cutoff shifts, ~9 us at N=16, but calibrating on a side stream like the real transfers would at least time the right path.

Hi @Etelis, thanks for the review.

Starting with 4, since it affects the rest. You were right, and I should have checked this at runtime before opening the PR.

The calibration was running on the legacy default stream (`0x0` at handler init, same inside `vllm serve`). `swap_blocks_batch` doesn't use `cuMemcpyBatchAsync` on that stream ([cache_kernels.cu#L163-L166](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5ea23ad9b80e8c22fc7a4f326a9e378f81639d84/csrc/libtorch_stable/cache_kernels.cu#L163-L166)) and falls back to one `cudaMemcpyAsync` per copy. So what I measured as "DMA" was the fallback, not the path real transfers take.

While checking this I found a second problem: inside a real server the calibration wasn't running at all. The worker's CPU tensors are strided views of the shared mmap region, and `measure_load_paths` returns None for non-contiguous tensors, so the handler just kept the defaults without logging anything. The numbers in the description are from a standalone worker with its own contiguous tensor, which is why I didn't notice.

Fixed in a0cc5ad4e. The calibration now runs on its own stream and reads the strided rows like real loads do. I added two tests that fail without the fix. 8eed6a0f4 adds the margin, more on that in 2.

The server now logs:
```
KV offload load path calibrated for 65536-byte copies in 122.7 ms: Triton from N=128 (default N=None); 
Triton/DMA time at N=16/32/64/128/256: 1.43 1.15 1.01 0.90 0.82
```

The numbers in the description are wrong because of this, so I'll update it. Results for 1-3 on the fixed code are in the next comment.

@Etelis Results for 1-3 on the fixed code: A30, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct TP1 (64 KiB pages), default `vllm serve` flags.

**1. Startup.** Launch to `/health`, median of 3. Calibration adds no measurable startup time.

| Triton cache | off | on | calibration itself |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| cold | 70.1 s | 70.1 s | 115-121 ms |
| warm | 53.7 s | 53.7 s | 58-63 ms |

**2. Margin and repeatability.** A path now has to be more than 5% faster at an N to override the default there (8eed6a0f4). Cutoff picked over repeated calibrations:

| copy size | before, 00d8649adc (25 runs) | after, 8eed6a0f4 (50 runs) |
|---:|---|---|
| 4 KiB | 16 / 32 | 64 |
| 8 KiB | 16 / 32 | 32 |
| 16 KiB | 16 / 32 | 16 |
| 32 KiB | 16 / 32 | 128 |
| 64 KiB | 16 / 32 | 128 |

"Before" is the code as I first posted it, which timed the per-copy fallback on the default stream (see my previous comment), so its values are wrong as well as unstable.

As you expected, the margin doesn't cover everything: in my test with two GPUs on one PCIe switch calibrating at the same time, 32/64 KiB still swung. **So e26e6e9d4 calibrates on rank 0 only, and every rank uses its result.** With TP=2 on those two GPUs, both ranks pick N=128 in 4 of 4 starts.

**3. Serving.** Every request loads a 256 MiB prefix from CPU (64 KiB copies: DMA with calibration off, Triton with it on). Median of 3 servers:

| | off | on |
|---|---:|---:|
| TTFT, concurrency 1 | 70.3 ms | 63.5 ms |
| TTFT, concurrency 8 | 206 ms | 179 ms |
| requests/s, concurrency 8 | 2.475 | 2.498 |
| TPOT, concurrency 8 | 23.9 ms | 23.8 ms |

TTFT improves by 10-13%, throughput by about 1%, and TPOT doesn't change.

<details>
<summary>Setup</summary>

- A30 (PCIe Gen4), torch 2.13.0+cu126, Triton 3.7.1, CUDA 12.8 forward-compat libcuda on a 535 kernel driver.
- Startup: cold means an empty `TRITON_CACHE_DIR`; the vLLM compile cache was warm in every run.
- Serving: 64 prefixes of 2048 tokens sent once, then 192 requests going through them in order with a fresh 32-token suffix, so each one misses the GPU cache and loads from CPU. `cpu_bytes_to_use` 32 GiB, 16 output tokens at concurrency 1, 128 at concurrency 8.

</details>

AI assistance (Claude) was used for the investigation, the fix and the measurements. I reviewed every changed line and ran everything above on my own hardware.

Ran the new head (13e7141a) calibration on a GB10 for comparison: `measure_load_paths` + `pick_min_n` standalone, 30 repeats per size, 128 KiB strided pinned rows, torch 2.12.1 / CUDA 13.0, unified memory so no PCIe.

Cutoff over 30 runs: 4 KiB 64 (30/30), 8 KiB 32 (30/30), 16 KiB 32 (29-30/30), 64 KiB 16 (30/30), 32 KiB 16 or 32 (10/20). Triton/DMA at N=16 / 256: 4 KiB 1.68 / 0.38, 16 KiB 1.13 / 0.24, 64 KiB 0.85 / 0.29. Two runs agree to ~0.03.

So repeatability holds here too, except 32 KiB where the N=16 ratio is 0.95, right on the margin. The bigger difference from your A30 table is at the large end: DMA batch is the slow side on this box, Triton is 3.4x faster at N=256 for 64 KiB, so calibration takes 64 KiB from DMA-only (default) to Triton from N=16, where A30 gets 128.

I added a `CopyBackend` interface in #59374. From a long-term perspective,
I wonder whether the DMA/Triton selection and calibration logic in this PR
could eventually be moved behind that interface.

This could make backend-specific benchmarking easier and leave more room for
future copy-path optimizations without adding more logic to the worker.

@Etelis, could you share your view on whether this layering makes sense?

```python
"""GH200 run of vllm #57569's load-path calibration, called the way the worker
calls it (gpu_worker._measure_min_n): copy size = page size,
chunk = min(next_pow2(page), 8192), host = a pinned CPU tensor whose rows are
read every other row. Usage: calib_57569.py REPEATS OUT.json [--extend]
--extend raises CALIBRATION_MAX_SCRATCH_BYTES so 128 and 256 KiB copies are
measured too (outside the PR's own cap; reported separately)."""
import collections
import json
import statistics
import sys
import time

import torch

import vllm.v1.kv_offload.cpu.swap_blocks_triton as sbt
from vllm import _custom_ops as ops
from vllm.triton_utils import triton

repeats, out_path = int(sys.argv[1]), sys.argv[2]
extend = "--extend" in sys.argv
sizes = [4096, 8192, 16384, 32768, 65536]
if extend:
    sbt.CALIBRATION_MAX_SCRATCH_BYTES = 64 * 1024 * 1024
    sizes += [131072, 262144]
dev = torch.device("cuda:0")
host = torch.empty((1024, 256 * 1024), dtype=torch.int8).pin_memory()


def bandwidth(size: int, chunk: int, n: int = 256, reps: int = 20) -> dict:
    """Median GB/s of each path for n copies of `size` bytes, same setup as
    measure_load_paths (every other host row, dedicated stream)."""
    scratch = torch.empty(n * size, dtype=torch.int8, device=dev)
    idx = torch.arange(n, dtype=torch.int64)
    src = (host.data_ptr() + 2 * host.stride(0) * idx).pin_memory()
    dst = (scratch.data_ptr() + size * idx).pin_memory()
    z = torch.full((n,), size, dtype=torch.int64).pin_memory()
    paths = {
        "dma": lambda: ops.swap_blocks_batch(src, dst, z, is_src_access_order_any=True),
        "triton": lambda: sbt.swap_blocks_batch(src, dst, z, bytes_per_chunk=chunk, min_n=0),
    }
    res = {}
    with torch.cuda.stream(torch.cuda.Stream(device=dev)):
        for name, fn in paths.items():
            fn()
            ts = []
            for _ in range(reps):
                torch.accelerator.synchronize()
                t0 = time.perf_counter()
                fn()
                torch.accelerator.synchronize()
                ts.append(time.perf_counter() - t0)
            res[name] = round(n * size / statistics.median(ts) / 1e9, 1)
    return res


out = {"device": torch.cuda.get_device_name(0), "torch": torch.__version__,
       "repeats": repeats, "extend": extend, "sizes": {}}
for size in sizes:
    chunk = min(triton.next_power_of_2(size), 8192)
    default = sbt.default_min_n(size)
    picks, runs, ms = [], [], []
    for _ in range(repeats):
        t0 = time.perf_counter()
        r = sbt.measure_load_paths(size, chunk, host, dev)
        ms.append((time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1e3)
        assert r is not None, f"not measurable at {size}"
        runs.append(r)
        picks.append(sbt.pick_min_n(r, default))
    med = [round(statistics.median(x), 2) for x in zip(*runs)]
    out["sizes"][size] = {
        "chunk": chunk, "default_min_n": default,
        "picks": {str(k): v for k, v in collections.Counter(picks).items()},
        "median_ratio_triton_over_dma": dict(zip(map(str, sbt.CALIBRATION_NS), med)),
        "ratio_min_max": [[round(min(x), 2), round(max(x), 2)] for x in zip(*runs)],
        "calibration_ms_first_median": [round(ms[0], 1), round(statistics.median(ms), 1)],
        "gbps_at_n256": bandwidth(size, chunk),
    }
    print(size, out["sizes"][size], flush=True)
json.dump(out, open(out_path, "w"), indent=1)
```

detail.body:
## Purpose

Part of #57555. Stacked on #57343, so the first two commits here are from that PR.

**Updated 2026-10-05:** the first version timed the default-stream fallback instead of `cuMemcpyBatchAsync`, and inside a server it didn't run at all ([details](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57569#issuecomment-5981553144)). Fixed in a0cc5ad4e; 8eed6a0f4 adds a 5% margin and e26e6e9d4 calibrates on rank 0 only. The numbers below are re-measured inside `vllm serve`.

The CPU→GPU load path picks between `cuMemcpyBatchAsync` and the Triton kernel with two constants tuned on one H100 (`THRESHOLD_BYTES = 28 KiB`, `MIN_N = 16`). The numbers in #57555 (H100, A30, GB10) show that where the two paths cross depends on the copy size, the batch size and the machine, so this lets a worker measure it instead.

With `"calibrate_load_path": true` in `kv_connector_extra_config`, rank 0 times both paths when the offloading worker is created, for its copy sizes, at N = 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, on a dedicated stream like real transfers. Every rank then uses the smallest N from which Triton is more than 5% faster at every larger N; where the two are within 5%, the default decides. If Triton never gets there the handler stays on DMA. The source is the real pinned CPU tensor and the destination is a scratch GPU buffer (at most 16 MiB), so no KV block is written. Copy sizes above 64 KiB would need a bigger scratch and are not measured. If anything goes wrong (no room for the scratch, host region too small, the op raising) the handler keeps the defaults and logs a warning.

The worker init is the natural place for this: the real GPU tensors, the pinned host region and the copy sizes all exist there, the GPU is idle, and `_select_swap_blocks_fn` already runs at that point.

To carry the result, the size cutoff and `MIN_N` are resolved into one `min_n` per handler at init and passed to the Triton wrapper, which still does a single comparison per call. With the option off the values are the same as today, so the default behaviour does not change.

On handlers with more than one copy size (the point @hclsys raised in #57555): one transfer sends all of a handler's sizes in a single call, so the per-size results are reduced to one. I kept that conservative, the largest `min_n`, and DMA for everything if any size never wins on Triton, which is what `max(sizes)` does today. When the sizes disagree the handler logs it, so it is visible how often this happens. Splitting the call by size is left for a follow-up once there is data from a hybrid model.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_swap_blocks_triton.py \
    tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_gpu_worker.py \
    tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_canonical_layout.py \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_canonical_mapping.py \
    tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering -q
pre-commit run --files <the 7 changed files>
```

New tests:

- `test_batches_below_min_n_use_dma`: the wrapper falls back to DMA below the `min_n` it is given (runs without CUDA).
- `test_pick_min_n`: Triton taking over at N=64, ahead everywhere, never ahead, a win at N=32 that doesn't count because N=64 loses again, and cells within the 5% margin left to the default.
- `test_measure_load_paths_times_every_probed_n`: times every probed N on a real pinned tensor, and returns nothing when the host region is too small.
- `test_measure_load_paths_reads_strided_host_rows`: measures on a strided view like the shared offload region (fails on the first version).
- `test_measure_load_paths_avoids_default_stream`: both paths are timed off the default stream (fails on the first version).
- `test_calibrated_load_path_uses_measured_min_n`: the measured value replaces the default, also for a 32 KiB page that defaults to DMA, the handler stays on DMA when Triton never wins, and a size the calibration didn't cover keeps its default.
- `test_calibration_failure_keeps_defaults`: an exception or a skipped measurement leaves `MIN_N`.
- `test_calibration_runs_on_rank0_only`: only rank 0 measures, and every rank gets its result.
- `test_mixed_copy_sizes_reduce_to_one_min_n`: the largest `min_n` is used, and one DMA-only size keeps the handler on DMA.

## Test Result

A30, PCIe Gen4, torch 2.13.0+cu126, Triton 3.7.1, editable install with `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1`, CUDA 12.8 forward-compat libcuda on a 535 kernel driver.

- The test files above: 482 passed, 2 skipped.
- All pre-commit hooks pass on the changed files, including mypy.

The rest is `vllm serve` with Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct TP1 (64 KiB pages) and default flags.

Startup cost. Launch to `/health`, median of 3. Cold means an empty `TRITON_CACHE_DIR`:

| Triton cache | off | on | calibration itself |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| cold | 70.1 s | 70.1 s | 115-121 ms |
| warm | 53.7 s | 53.7 s | 58-63 ms |

No measurable change. The +0.5-1 s I first reported came from a standalone `CPUOffloadingWorker`, where it was mostly the first Triton launch of a fresh process.

What it picked on this GPU, the same in 50 of 50 calibrations per size. N is the number of copies in one load call (blocks × layers); below the cutoff a load stays on DMA.

| copy size | default | calibrated |
|---:|---|---|
| 4 KiB | Triton from N=16 | Triton from N=64 |
| 8 KiB | Triton from N=16 | Triton from N=32 |
| 16 KiB | Triton from N=16 | Triton from N=16 |
| 32 KiB | DMA | Triton from N=128 |
| 64 KiB | DMA | Triton from N=128 |
| 128 KiB | DMA | not measured, DMA |

Serving. Every request loads a 256 MiB prefix from CPU (64 KiB copies: DMA with calibration off, Triton with it on), median of 3 servers:

With `TieringOffloadingSpec`, a CPU promotion is self-describing when a local request observes its primary-tier `HIT` before event translation; otherwise its stored event may retain the placeholder, while a later `HIT` can backfill metadata for removal. Ran the calibration on GB10 (sm_121, 121.7 GiB unified, aarch64, CUDA 13, torch 2.12.1+cu130), driving `measure_load_paths` / `pick_min_n` directly at `00d8649adc`. This branch touches no C++ against my build base, so the prebuilt `swap_blocks_batch` applies.

It does not return the same answer twice. Same function, same pinned host tensor, same process, seven consecutive calls per size:

```
CALIBRATION_REPS = 5 (as shipped)
   4K   min_n: [64, 64, 32, 64, 16, 64, 64]
  16K   min_n: [32, 16, 256, 32, 16, 64, 256]
  32K   min_n: [256, 16, 32, 32, 256, 64, 64]
  64K   min_n: [32, 16, 16, 128, 128, 256, 128]

CALIBRATION_REPS = 25
   4K   min_n: [64, 32, 32, 32, 16, 16, 16]
  16K   min_n: [16, 32, 16, 16, 16, 16, 16]
  32K   min_n: [32, 32, 16, 16, 16, 64, 64]
  64K   min_n: [128, 256, 128, 32, 32, 32, 128]
```

Five times the reps tightens 16 KiB but not 64 KiB, so this isn't only a rep-count problem.

The underlying medians at 16 KiB, six runs:

```
run   arm    N=16     N=32     N=64     N=128    N=256
0     dma    0.0489   0.0790   0.1292   0.2434   0.5520
0     tri    0.0473   0.0382   0.0381   0.0752   0.0928
3     dma    0.0483   0.0771   0.1261   0.2300   0.4388
3     tri    0.2140   0.1979   0.1275   0.1086   0.1234
```

The DMA arm is steady to about 2%. The Triton arm's median at N=16 moves between 0.037 and 0.25 ms across identical calls, roughly 6x, and it is right at that N that the crossing gets decided.

What I ruled out before blaming variance: the co-tenant on this card holds 16.9 GB but is not computing (utilization sampled at 0-1%), and the SM clock sits at 2411 MHz with the part at 53 C for the whole run, so no throttle. It is not JIT either, since `run_ms` already discards a warm-up and the fast runs are as often first as last.

The reduction then amplifies it. `pick_min_n` walks down from the largest N and breaks on the first `tri > dma`, with no tolerance, so one cell landing the wrong side of 1.0 at N=128 or 256 truncates the whole walk. That is how 16 KiB gets both 16 and 256 out of the same machine minutes apart.

Two things that might help, in the order I'd try them:

- require a margin rather than `tri > dma`, so a cell within noise of parity doesn't break the walk
- repeat the whole measurement two or three times and take the consensus pick, rather than more reps inside one measurement

I also tried a variant with the destination slots permuted instead of contiguous, since real loads write scattered block ids and the contiguous scratch is friendlier to the copy engine than production is. The run-to-run spread above swamps it, so I have nothing to report there yet, and it seems worth settling the stability first.

Caveats: one machine, load direction only, nothing above 64 KiB, and I drove the two functions directly rather than through a real serve, so I have not seen what a handler picks in situ.

swap_blocks_batch only takes cuMemcpyBatchAsync when the current stream isn't stream 0 (`usable_stream` in cache_kernels.cu), otherwise it loops cudaMemcpyAsync. I couldn't find anything on the init path that sets a stream, so measure_load_paths times the loop. Checked with VLLM_KV_OFFLOAD_MAX_BATCH_DESCRIPTORS=1 (only chunks the batch path): N=256 x 4 KiB goes 0.128 -> 0.412 ms on a side stream, default stream 0.44 -> 0.49, so it isn't using it.

measure_load_paths as is vs inside `with torch.cuda.stream(torch.cuda.Stream())`, DMA ms at N=16 / N=256:

4 KiB   0.035 / 0.439  vs  0.018 / 0.125
16 KiB  0.033 / 0.424  vs  0.035 / 0.286

Starting with 4, since it affects the rest. You were right, and I should have checked this at runtime before opening the PR.

The calibration was running on the legacy default stream (`0x0` at handler init, same inside `vllm serve`). `swap_blocks_batch` doesn't use `cuMemcpyBatchAsync` on that stream ([cache_kernels.cu#L163-L166](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5ea23ad9b80e8c22fc7a4f326a9e378f81639d84/csrc/libtorch_stable/cache_kernels.cu#L163-L166)) and falls back to one `cudaMemcpyAsync` per copy. The worker's CPU tensors are strided views of the shared mmap region, and `measure_load_paths` returns None for non-contiguous tensors, so the handler just kept the defaults without logging anything. Thanks for taking this on. When we originally wrote the Triton path, we expected the best copy-size and batch-size thresholds to vary across hardware, so it makes sense to revisit the fixed values.

Before merging, I'd like to understand a few things:

1. You've measured worker construction in isolation. Could you also run a real deployment 2–3 times, with cold and warm Triton caches, and report how long calibration takes and how much it adds to total startup time?

2. I agree with @hclsys that we need a meaningful margin rather than comparing `tri > dma` directly. Given the variation they saw, could you also check whether repeating the whole calibration gives a consistent cutoff? A margin might help around parity without resolving the larger swings.

3. The supporting copy benchmarks show roughly 1.5–1.7x improvements in some cases. Could you run a serving workload that exercises KV offloading, with calibration enabled and disabled, and compare latency and throughput? I'd like to see how much of that copy improvement carries through to serving.

4. One thing I noticed reading the code: calibration doesn't explicitly select a transfer stream, while `swap_blocks_batch` falls back to individual copies on the legacy default stream. Could you verify that calibration uses a non-default CUDA stream, matching real offload transfers, so we're actually measuring `cuMemcpyBatchAsync`? I haven't checked this at runtime yet.

```python
"""GH200 run of vllm #57569's load-path calibration, called the way the worker
calls it (gpu_worker._measure_min_n): copy size = page size,
chunk = min(next_pow2(page), 8192), host = a pinned CPU tensor whose rows are
read every other row. Usage: calib_57569.py REPEATS OUT.json [--extend]
--extend raises CALIBRATION_MAX_SCRATCH_BYTES so 128 and 256 KiB copies are
measured too (outside the PR's own cap; reported separately)."""
import collections
import json
import statistics
import sys
import time

import torch

import vllm.v1.kv_offload.cpu.swap_blocks_triton as sbt
from vllm import _custom_ops as ops
from vllm.triton_utils import triton

repeats, out_path = int(sys.argv[1]), sys.argv[2]
extend = "--extend" in sys.argv
sizes = [4096, 8192, 16384, 32768, 65536]
if extend:
    sbt.CALIBRATION_MAX_SCRATCH_BYTES = 64 * 1024 * 1024
    sizes += [131072, 262144]
dev = torch.device("cuda:0")
host = torch.empty((1024, 256 * 1024), dtype=torch.int8).pin_memory()


def bandwidth(size: int, chunk: int, n: int = 256, reps: int = 20) -> dict:
    """Median GB/s of each path for n copies of `size` bytes, same setup as
    measure_load_paths (every other host row, dedicated stream)."""
    scratch = torch.empty(n * size, dtype=torch.int8, device=dev)
    idx = torch.arange(n, dtype=torch.int64)
    src = (host.data_ptr() + 2 * host.stride(0) * idx).pin_memory()
    dst = (scratch.data_ptr() + size * idx).pin_memory()
    z = torch.full((n,), size, dtype=torch.int64).pin_memory()
    paths = {
        "dma": lambda: ops.swap_blocks_batch(src, dst, z, is_src_access_order_any=True),
        "triton": lambda: sbt.swap_blocks_batch(src, dst, z, bytes_per_chunk=chunk, min_n=0),
    }
    res = {}
    with torch.cuda.stream(torch.cuda.Stream(device=dev)):
        for name, fn in paths.items():
            fn()
            ts = []
            for _ in range(reps):
                torch.accelerator.synchronize()
                t0 = time.perf_counter()
                fn()
                torch.accelerator.synchronize()
                ts.append(time.perf_counter() - t0)
            res[name] = round(n * size / statistics.median(ts) / 1e9, 1)
    return res


out = {"device": torch.cuda.get_device_name(0), "torch": torch.__version__,
       "repeats": repeats, "extend": extend, "sizes": {}}
for size in sizes:
    chunk = min(triton.next_power_of_2(size), 8192)
    default = sbt.default_min_n(size)
    picks, runs, ms = [], [], []
    for _ in range(repeats):
        t0 = time.perf_counter()
        r = sbt.measure_load_paths(size, chunk, host, dev)
        ms.append((time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1e3)
        assert r is not None, f"not measurable at {size}"
        runs.append(r)
        picks.append(sbt.pick_min_n(r, default))
    med = [round(statistics.median(x), 2) for x in zip(*runs)]
    out["sizes"][size] = {
        "chunk": chunk, "default_min_n": default,
        "picks": {str(k): v for k, v in collections.Counter(picks).items()},
        "median_ratio_triton_over_dma": dict(zip(map(str, sbt.CALIBRATION_NS), med)),
        "ratio_min_max": [[round(min(x), 2), round(max(x), 2)] for x in zip(*runs)],
        "calibration_ms_first_median": [round(ms[0], 1), round(statistics.median(ms), 1)],
        "gbps_at_n256": bandwidth(size, chunk),
    }
    print(size, out["sizes"][size], flush=True)
json.dump(out, open(out_path, "w"), indent=1)
```
